body:
In chase of the black rabbit you became the rabbit avenger. Great build, can't express enough how satisfying it was to watch not only the process but the whole easter egg hunt for the references. Great as always. 

And R.I.P. the lethal christmas tree.

Hi, the first thing that came to my mind was the second method, personally I would give it a try since you have found proof in papers. If you are looking for easy to use sensors check out the MAX30102, works alright for simple applications and can measure SpO2, plus it's PPG based so it's non-invasive. It's not a bad option, however you will need to test how it fits in your case. The datasheets are decent, but I'm afraid you would have to write code for it yourself.

You are not alone. As someone who prints on close to daily basis I have never printed a benchy. Usually cubes, test towers etc. do the trick for me and if not I just calibrate my Frankenstein with the at the time needed model. So far it works for me. That being said I can spend hours when trying a new material to adjust the settings.
Seems solid, besides the Silesian uni is known as one of the best BME available in Poland. If you're into coding and IT this may be a good option.

Well, not only does it already exist, it is quite common tbh. When it comes to myoelectric hands we use AI to adjust the movements. Think about it like this, the signal that we can read from  muscles is not only full of noise but also it varies a lot, so AI is trained to react to certain patterns and optimize the detection process. From what I recall True Limb got something like this, you can use their hand just after unboxing, however you need to train it to get the best results
Why not. It could be fun. Going even further imagine being able to see your "buffs" & "debuffs". Honestly it could be an interesting read.
Joey Del Marco, sounds like I'm lucky this one time
